Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for evaluating Mr. Jason Miller, a 37-year-old gentleman who attended my clinic regarding longstanding integumentary features that have been present since birth. 

On examination, there is a total absence of scalp and body hair, along with a complete lack of eyebrows and no cilia present along either the upper or lower eyelid margins. Furthermore, his nails display severe dysplastic changes, with coarse longitudinal ridging, pronounced surface roughness, and abnormal plate architecture. Despite this, the fingernail plates remain firmly adherent, with no evidence of distal nail bed detachment. 

The remainder of the physical examination was largely unremarkable. Oral inspection revealed entirely normal teeth, with sound dental development and no enamel anomalies. Examination of the groin and external genitalia showed bilaterally descended testes without asymmetry or retention, and the inguinal canals were intact with no palpable protrusion or bulge. 

Mr. Miller works as an accountant, takes no routine medications, and maintains a healthy lifestyle. His vital signs were normal, including a blood pressure of 118/76 mmHg and a resting heart rate of 70 beats per minute. Cardiopulmonary auscultation and abdominal palpation were completely benign. His family history is non-contributory, with no relatives exhibiting similar hair or nail differences.

I would be grateful for your expert clinical opinion and any guidance you can provide regarding his ongoing management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Rachel Vance
